definitions.explanation: having or showing excessive interest in sexual pleasure
an appreciation of romantic or aesthetic beauty, especially in classical literature

examples.japanese: {好色|こうしょく}な{男|おとこ}だ。
{好色|こうしょく}な{目|め}つきで{女性|じょせい}を{見|み}る。
examples.english: He looks at women with lustful eyes.

examples.japanese: あの{上司|じょうし}は{好色|こうしょく}で{有名|ゆうめい}なので、{女性|じょせい}{社員|しゃいん}から{嫌|きら}われている。
examples.english: That boss is famous for being lecherous, so he is disliked by female employees.

examples.japanese: 『{好色|こうしょく}{一代|いちだい}{男|おとこ}』は{有名|ゆうめい}な{作品|さくひん}だ。
examples.english: The Life of an Amorous Man is a famous work.

examples.japanese: {井原|いはら}{西鶴|さいかく}の{好色|こうしょく}{物|もの}は{江戸|えど}{文学|ぶんがく}の{傑作|けっさく}だ。
examples.english: Ihara Saikaku's amorous tales are masterpieces of Edo literature.

examples.japanese: {古典|こてん}{文学|ぶんがく}における{好色|こうしょく}の{概念|がいねん}は、{現代|げんだい}とは{異|こと}なる{意味合|いみあ}いを{持|も}っていた。
examples.english: The concept of koushoku in classical literature had a different nuance from its modern meaning.

notes:
Refers to excessive sexual desire or lechery in modern usage, but in classical Japanese literature it carried a broader, more aestheticized meaning closer to "the pursuit of romantic beauty."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {好色|こうしょく}な{男|おとこ} — lecherous man
- {好色|こうしょく}な{目|め}つき — lustful gaze
- {好色|こうしょく}{漢|かん} — lecher, womanizer
- {好色|こうしょく}{家|か} — libertine, rake

LITERARY CONTEXT:
{井原|いはら}{西鶴|さいかく}'s {好色|こうしょく}{一代|いちだい}{男|おとこ} (The Life of an Amorous Man, 1682) established {好色|こうしょく}{物|もの} (amorous tales) as a major genre of Edo-period fiction. In this classical context, {好色|こうしょく} implied a sophisticated appreciation of romantic encounters rather than crude lust.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {色欲|しきよく} — sexual desire (blunt, negative)
- {淫乱|いんらん} — lewdness (strongly negative)
- {助平|すけべい} — pervert, lecher (colloquial, mildly humorous)
- {女好|おんなず}き — womanizer (everyday, informal)
